questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), calculate the difference between India’s share of world exports of rice in 2010 and 2022. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 1 and Figure 2) show that the rice export ban by India in 2022 is likely to have had a significant impact on the world price of rice.

Extract B (line 19) states: ‘In Nigeria, the demand for rice is very price inelastic’. With the help of a diagram, explain how the Indian export ban is likely to have affected the market for rice in Nigeria.

Extract C (lines 6–7) states: ‘An alternative would be to impose a maximum price for consumers, as both Sri Lanka and the Philippines have done’. Using the data and your knowledge of economics, evaluate the view that imposing a maximum price for rice is the best way for a rice-importing nation, such as Nigeria, to ensure the affordability of a basic food for its citizens.
Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the median number of storm overflow hours by water company in 2022.
Explain how the data in Extract D (Figure 4) show that household water bills have increased in real terms since privatisation in 1989.

Extract E (line 10) states: ‘The minimum efficient scale in the water industry is large’. With the help of a diagram, explain why the large minimum efficient scale in the water industry is likely to lead to the market being supplied by a few large firms with monopoly power.

Extract F (lines 5–6) states: ‘if regulators impose fines, these costs may be passed on to consumers or reduce investment’. Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that stronger regulation would be a better policy than bringing the water industry back into public ownership.
Explain, with examples, the differences between a private good, a public good and a quasi-public good.
Evaluate the view that oligopolies serve society well.
Explain how technological progress can affect productivity, efficiency and firms’ costs of production.
Assess the view that the main objective of firms is to maximise profits.
Explain the factors that determine a firm’s demand for labour.
Assess the view that a national minimum wage, such as the UK’s National Living Wage, contributes to an improvement in economic welfare.

Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), calculate how the value of the Norwegian krone has changed compared to the Singapore dollar between 26 October 2021 and 29 May 2023. Give your answer as a percentage and to one decimal place.
Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 2) show that Singapore may have benefitted from managing its exchange rate compared to Germany and Norway.

Extract B (lines 6–7) states: ‘Some analysts hope that, before long, the currency will start to appreciate which could help Norway reduce inflation.’ With the help of a suitable diagram, explain how an appreciation of the krone could help Norway reduce inflation.

Extract C (lines 1–2) states: ‘An economy that has seen considerable success by intervening in the foreign exchange market to manage its currency is Singapore.’ Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that an economy is likely to perform better with a managed exchange rate rather than a freely floating exchange rate.
Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the difference between the percentage increase in GDP for Japan and the USA between 2001 and 2023. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Explain how the data in Extract D (Figure 3) show how Ethiopia has developed at a faster rate than Japan since 2001.

Extract E (lines 15–17) states: ‘In recent years, some of the BRICS+ countries, including China and India, have been responsible for large foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows into the G7.’ With the help of a suitable diagram, explain how increased inward foreign direct investment (FDI) can affect a country’s level of employment.

Extract F (lines 1–2) states: ‘While some see the benefits of the emergence of the BRICS+ economies, others are more worried by their rapid economic growth.’ Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that the continued rapid economic growth of the BRICS+ economies is likely to be damaging to the macroeconomic performance of G7 nations, such as the UK.
Explain factors that may lead to an increase in a country’s national debt as a percentage of GDP.
Assess the view that raising direct taxes to finance an increase in government spending is better than raising indirect taxes.
Explain how supply-side policies can help to achieve a low, stable rate of inflation.
Evaluate the view that a low rate of inflation is always beneficial for a country’s macroeconomic performance.
Explain the main limitations of using national income data to assess differences in living standards between countries.
Assess the view that economic development in LEDCs is best achieved through interventionist strategies.
Which one of the following best describes mandated choice?
options: A limited range of options is provided
Individuals are required by law to choose an option
Options are framed to influence the outcome of decisions
The option is selected automatically if an alternative is not chosen

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows a production possibility diagram for an economy where goods and services are produced in the private and public sectors. The economy is currently producing at point Y. Following a change in government, it is decided that the output of public sector goods and services should be increased by VW. What is the opportunity cost, in terms of private sector output, of this reallocation of resources?
options: OS
OT
ST
YZ

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best describes how a social scientist would develop an economic theory?
options: Apply logic to make connections between normative and positive economic concepts
Create a hypothesis and test whether it can predict the behaviour of economic agents
Develop a number of policies and test whether they are successful in the real world
Form a set of value judgements and test whether they are supported by statistical data

questions.questionText: Which one of the following diagrams, A, B, C or D, shows the impact on an economy of a permanent reduction in an indirect tax?
Which one of the following is most likely to lead to an increase in the number of people who are frictionally unemployed in the UK?
options: A fall in the number of Jobcentres provided by the government
A persistent fall in reported levels of consumer confidence
A reduction in the rate at which Jobseeker’s Allowance is paid
A significant real terms increase in the National Living Wage

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to indicate that a government is trying to cause a significant change in the pattern of economic activity?
options: A reduction in the rate of tax on income from retirement pensions
A reduction in the tax on a good with positive consumption externalities
An increase in the rate of an inheritance tax
An increase in the tax on a good with very inelastic demand

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the amount of capital, land and labour employed and the output of a firm before and after it expands to increase its productive capacity. Which one of the following do the data in Table 1 show has resulted from the expansion?
options: Diseconomies of scale
Falling labour productivity
Increasing marginal returns
Increasing returns to scale

questions.questionText: An entrepreneur, and sole owner, has £300 000 invested in a firm. The same investment would generate an annual rate of return of 35% if it was transferred to a different market. Table 2 shows the firm’s annual total costs of production, not including the opportunity cost of the capital the entrepreneur has invested, and annual total revenue in the current market. How much abnormal profit is the business making each year in its current market?

Land is an example of a resource that is in composite demand. Land can be used to produce soya beans and for forestry. Between January 2019 and January 2024, the market price of soya beans increased by almost 40%. This was largely driven by the rise in demand for soya beans. Which one of the following diagrams, A, B, C or D, shows the most likely effect of the increase in demand for soya beans on the market for land that is used for forestry?
Which one of the following best explains the operation of the accelerator process?
options: An increase in investment leads to a larger increase in national income
An increase in productive capacity leads to a larger change in investment
The growth of productive capacity depends on the growth in investment
The level of investment depends on the rate of change in national income

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the long-run trend rate of unemployment and the actual rate of unemployment in a country over a period of time. At which one of the following points was the economy most likely to be in the recession phase of its economic cycle?
options: Point A
Point B
Point C
Point D

questions.questionText: Table 3 shows the value of the Human Development Index (HDI) for three countries in 2021 and figures from the index’s health and education dimensions. It can be deduced from Table 3 that in 2021
options: Finland had a faster rate of growth than the UK.
Finland’s Human Development Index was 1.1% higher than the UK’s.
Ireland’s gross national income per capita was higher than Finland’s.
Ireland had a more equitable distribution of income than Finland.

questions.questionText: Figure 3 below shows the supply curve (S) for cakes. Which one of the following can be concluded from Figure 3? The supply of cakes
options: is less price inelastic when price increases from £8 to £10 than when it increases from £10 to £15.
is more price inelastic when price increases from £8 to £10 than when it increases from £10 to £15.
is price elastic when the price increases from £8 to £10 and when it increases from £10 to £15.
is unitary price elastic when price increases from £8 to £10 and when it increases from £10 to £15.

questions.questionText: Figure 4 shows a market for houses to rent. The current average monthly rent in the market is R1. Why is this market in disequilibrium at an average monthly rent of R1?
options: Market forces are likely to encourage landlords to reduce the rent they charge
Market forces are likely to lead to an increase in the average rent and fewer houses available for tenants
Some landlords who would like to rent houses out at R1 cannot find tenants
Some potential tenants who would like to rent a house at R1 cannot find a house to rent

questions.questionText: A large company experiences a significant fall in its year-end profits. Reports suggest it is a consequence of the divorce of ownership from control within the company. Which one of the following is most likely to explain why the divorce of ownership from control may have harmed the firm’s performance?
options: As part of their earnings, managers receive profit-related pay and share options
Due to the satisficing principle, managers act in the interests of shareholders
Moral hazard means shareholders take more risks to achieve greater rewards
Profit maximisation is not the most important objective for all managers

questions.questionText: Table 4 shows the index of consumer prices and the unemployment rate for an economy. The data is for the end of each quarter in a particular year. The index of consumer prices for the final quarter of the previous year was 120.9. According to the data, it can be concluded that
options: prices were lower at the start of the year and employment was lower at the end of the year.
the quarterly inflation rate fluctuated whilst the unemployment rate increased throughout the year.
the relationship between the change in the inflation and unemployment rates was positive in each quarter.
there was an inverse relationship between prices and unemployment in each quarter.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to be included in a broad measure of the money supply but not in a narrow measure of the money supply?
options: Commercial banks’ deposits with the central bank
Notes and coins held by households
Savings deposited with commercial banks that have more than a year to maturity
The total amount owed on credit cards that has been outstanding for more than 28 days

questions.questionText: Table 5 shows the liquidity ratio and capital ratio for two, otherwise identical, banks. All other things being equal, it is likely that
options: Bank Y is less profitable than Bank Z and is less secure.
Bank Y is less profitable than Bank Z but is more secure.
Bank Y is more profitable than Bank Z and is more secure.
Bank Y is more profitable than Bank Z but is less secure.

questions.questionText: Figure 5 shows the average cost (AC), marginal cost (MC), average revenue (AR) and marginal revenue (MR) curves for a firm in a perfectly competitive market. The entry of new firms shifts the AR and MR curves from AR1 = MR1 to AR2 = MR2. All other things being equal, which one of the following combinations of statements would be correct for a profit-maximising firm?

Figure 6 shows the average revenue (AR), marginal revenue (MR) and marginal cost (MC) curves of a train-operating firm for peak-time and off-peak passengers. It also shows the price (P1) that all passengers currently pay. The train-operating firm introduces price discrimination to maximise profits. What is the effect on consumer surplus?
options: Falls for both off-peak and peak-time passengers
Falls for off-peak passengers and rises for peak-time passengers
Falls for peak-time passengers and rises for off-peak passengers
Rises for both off-peak and peak-time passengers

questions.questionText: Table 6 shows the size of the UK labour force and the percentage of the labour force belonging to a trade union in 2012 and 2022. According to the data in Table 6, what is the percentage fall, to one decimal place, in the number of workers belonging to a trade union between 2012 and 2022?
Table 7 shows four situations in which one group of workers earns less than another and states the reason given by employers. Which one is the best example of wage discrimination?
Which one of the following is most likely to lead to individuals who are currently in relative poverty remaining in relative poverty?
options: A major housebuilding programme helps to reduce the number of workers who are geographically immobile
Average earnings in an economy rise more slowly than the increase in the national minimum wage
The government changes the income tax system in a country to make it more progressive
The rate of increase in the price of necessities, such as energy, is higher than for all goods and services

questions.questionText: Country X and Country Y have identical amounts of the factors of production that can be used to produce either canoes or rowing boats. Figure 7 shows the production possibility frontiers (PPFs) for the two countries. Which one of the following is supported by the data in Figure 7?
options: Country X has both an absolute advantage and a comparative advantage in producing canoes
In Country Y, the production of rowing boats requires two and a half times as many resources as the production of canoes
The maximum number of canoes and rowing boats that Country X and Country Y can produce between them is 400
The opportunity cost of producing a canoe in Country Y is 25% lower than it is in Country X

questions.questionText: Figure 8 shows the domestic demand (Dd) and supply (Sd) curves for paper in a country. Figure 8 also shows the world supply curve when the country does not have any restrictions on imports of paper (Sw) and the world supply curve when a tariff of $10 per unit is imposed on paper imported from the rest of the world (Swt). Following the introduction of the tariff, what is the change in the amount the country has to pay to the rest of the world for the paper it imports?
options: US$2300 million
US$3300 million
US$4050 million
US$5200 million

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a supply-side policy that is most likely to lead to an improvement in the balance of trade in goods and services on the current account of the UK’s balance of payments?
options: A significant and sustained reduction in Bank Rate by the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of England
Deregulation that makes it easier for UK transnational corporations to invest abroad
Increasing the supply of pounds on the foreign exchange market to reduce the exchange rate and make exports cheaper
Tax breaks for manufacturing firms that invest in upgrading their machinery and other capital goods

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements regarding UK competition policy is correct?
